purpose: Bounded World Bank WDR2026 route from AI adoption through local complements and value-chain concentration to public capacity and state-dependence questions, preserving realized capability and external-response gaps.

events.geography: Global/developing-country analytical frame with US-relevant value-chain and institutional comparison implications
events.date_precision: World Development Report 2026 framework and chapter synthesis; exact country adoption dates and external responses are not retained
events.denominator: One World Bank flagship analytical framework and chapter-level evidence; technology, country, firm, and agency units are not pooled
events.method: World Bank synthesis of research, country evidence, technology-diffusion comparisons, value-chain analysis, and public-sector capability discussion
events.missingness: Realized country adoption, supplier switching, infrastructure outage, public-service outcome, worker/household incidence, ownership, bargaining, and external actor response are not retained
events.exposure: The report frames AI capability through adopt–adapt–advance pathways and identifies infrastructure, skills, institutions, data, and local-language fit as complements
events.alternatives_before_action: Alternative providers, open standards, local adaptation, procurement choices, replacement time, and ability to refuse or switch are identified as questions rather than observed episode fields
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: AI tools can expand access and public/firm capability, while hardware, infrastructure, models, and applications remain concentrated across countries and companies
events.choice_or_response: The report identifies dependency, capital concentration, surveillance, propaganda, public-budget pressure, and regulatory-capacity gaps as governance risks; it does not observe a specific state response
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Countries, governments, firms, public agencies, and individuals hold different positions in the value chain; control over models, chips, data centers, data, procurement, and enforcement is not measured for one case
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Adopt–adapt–advance policy and governance recommendations are visible, but no completed procurement correction, public-service remedy, or accountability outcome is linked
events.immediate_outcome: The framework establishes a capability/dependence mechanism in which local complements and concentrated value chains jointly shape usable AI capacity
events.protected_outcome: Local adaptation and public capacity could improve service or productive capability, but no realized household, worker, or state protection is measured
events.sacrificed_outcome: Dependency and concentration could reduce replaceability, bargaining room, privacy, or public control, but no realized loss or affected actor is measured
events.cost_risk_transfer: The report does not identify how infrastructure, capital, data, energy, governance, or correction costs transfer among firms, households, governments, and foreign suppliers
events.later_outcome: No linked country capability, public-service quality, outage/switching, alliance, trade, bargaining, or geopolitical behavior outcome is observed
events.meaning_and_attribution: The framework makes control, dependency, and capability political questions but does not measure public legitimacy, trust, blame, or identity in a named episode
events.public_or_collective_response: Policy recommendations and governance categories are reported; public action, regulatory enforcement, supplier response, and external actor behavior remain open
events.counterexample: Imported tools can deliver useful capability without frontier-model production, and concentration can lower entry costs even while dependency risk persists
events.source_and_uncertainty: World Bank analytical framework and report synthesis; no single effect size, US estimate, supplier concentration measure, or realized geopolitical response is established

arrows.to: adoption through infrastructure, skills, institutions, data, and local fit
arrows.evidence: The report's adopt–adapt–advance framework identifies local complements as conditions for productive capability rather than treating exposure alone as adoption
arrows.counterexample: Imported tools may provide useful capability without local frontier production, and complements may be present without effective adoption
arrows.remaining_gap: Country/firm episode with adoption date, complements, task/service use, cost, and realized output

arrows.evidence: The report identifies concentration across hardware, infrastructure, models, and applications and names dependency as a governance risk
arrows.counterexample: Open standards, procurement diversity, local adaptation, and cooperation may reduce dependency without eliminating concentration
arrows.remaining_gap: Supplier concentration, switching time/cost, outage or substitution event, ownership/control, and affected actor

arrows.to: public-service quality, legitimacy, and household outcome
arrows.evidence: The report lists public-service applications and a front-end evaluation gap but does not observe a service recipient outcome
arrows.counterexample: Back-end analytical capacity can improve while front-end access, correction, or trust remains unchanged or worsens
arrows.remaining_gap: Named agency/service episode with procurement, staff capacity, user access, error, correction, outcome, and trust

arrows.from: domestic AI capability and infrastructure dependence
arrows.to: state bargaining room and external response
arrows.evidence: The report identifies political power relationships among states, firms, governments, and individuals but no dated change in another actor's choice
arrows.counterexample: Capability can expand while a state remains dependent, or cooperation can turn dependence into mutual benefit rather than leverage
arrows.remaining_gap: Realized capability, replaceability, affected partner/supplier, and dated concession, refusal, substitution, or policy response

arrows.to: worker, household, public legitimacy, or geopolitical consequence
arrows.evidence: The framework supplies mechanisms and policy questions but no same-unit worker, household, public, or external response endpoint
arrows.counterexample: Higher capability may coexist with lower local control or burden, while dependency may coexist with useful access and welfare gains
arrows.remaining_gap: Linked domestic incidence, institutional remedy, trust/action, and external behavior after realized capability

boundary: This ledger formalizes a World Bank capability/dependence framework. It does not establish a US AI adoption rate, realized public-service improvement, supplier switching cost, state bargaining leverage, household benefit, or geopolitical consequence.
storage_boundary: Only the published World Bank framework, qualitative mechanisms, source metadata, and interpretation limits are retained; report inputs and restricted country/firms files are not stored.
